clue.text: Miss Mackenzie was his harlot, according to hearsay

indicators.note: hearsay is what people say aloud, so the word for harlot is taken by its sound

parts.note: a harlot is a trollop, a woman of loose morals

explanation.surface: Someone describes a novel's heroine as a fallen woman, passing on gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Mackenzie is an 1865 novel by the Victorian writer, whose surname is said the same as TROLLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel Miss Mackenzie was written by this Victorian novelist, so the heroine was his creation.

clue.text: Old land featuring in books on Ascension Island

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
to land a catch is to bag it

explanation.surface: An old country features in literature about Ascension Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascension Island' looks like the definition; Ascension is the reversal sign and Island alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, partner of Trinidad.

clue.text: Girl writer and old boy going with nurse around Rhode Island

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A woman author and a former pupil go with a nurse around an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Edna O'Brien wrote The Country Girls, hence 'Girl writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna O'Brien is the Irish novelist whose first book was The Country Girls.

clue.text: "Madame, I have become a whore through good-will and — through virtue" (Marquis de Sade)

definitions.text: "Madame, I have become a whore through good-will and — through virtue" (Marquis de Sade)

parts.words: "Madame, I have become a whore through good-will and — through virtue" (Marquis de Sade)
parts.note: the missing word from Sade, a noun for a dissolute person who rejects moral restraint

explanation.definitionFit: Sade's line pairs whore with a word for a debauched person free of moral rules.

clue.text: One like Erika Kohut dashed a certain hope

indicators.note: dashed hopes are smashed, so these words are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Somebody resembling a fictional woman has her particular hope crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Erika Kohut is the heroine of Elfriede Jelinek's novel The Piano Teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelinek's Erika Kohut teaches keyboard at a Vienna conservatory.

clue.text: British genuine left-wing writer

parts.note: echt is a German loanword in English meaning authentic

explanation.surface: A truly socialist author from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The German dramatist was a committed Marxist playwright and poet.

clue.text: Extend loan of book on the subject of novel

parts.note: re means concerning, about
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: A library user extends a book's borrowing time while talking about a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Library borrowers renew a book to keep it for longer.

clue.text: Daily Mail regularly goes with article on new royal aide

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner, a char

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tabloid goes along with a piece on a fresh palace assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily Mail' looks like the newspaper; a daily is British slang for a cleaning lady, a char. Charmian is Cleopatra's attendant in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmian is a waiting-woman to Queen Cleopatra in Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Song Trio perhaps cut with contrary Yankee fellow

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: a trio is an example of three

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A trio's number is shortened alongside an awkward American man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns Y and DON together, giving NODY.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song or ode of lament for the dead.

clue.text: Boozers taking on Swedish band for a nicker

indicators.note: the drinking places take on, or admit, the band, so it goes inside them

parts.note: boozers are pubs, also called bars
ABBA is the famous Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: Pubs hire a Swedish pop act at a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a nicker' looks like British slang for a pound; nicker here is a thief, and the Gospel robber Barabbas was released instead of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels this man is a robber, and a nicker is someone who steals.

clue.text: Prejudiced description of Othello's hair?

definitions.meaning: Othello is a Moor, so his hair is dark, not fair

explanation.definitionFit: Biased treatment is unjust; a Moor's hair would not be blond.

clue.text: McCarthy critic hammered a rum thriller

indicators.note: hammered means beaten out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A strange thriller gets panned by reviewers.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Miller's The Crucible attacked McCarthyism, and he defied the House Un-American Activities Committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Miller's The Crucible criticised Senator McCarthy's anti-communist witch-hunts.

clue.text: Writer from Athens? Not quite right

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a letter short of complete

parts.note: something from Athens is Greek, the question mark flagging the example

explanation.surface: Is this author really Athenian? Not entirely correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist author of The Female Eunuch.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer is an author and critic, best known for The Female Eunuch.

clue.text: A wan room's not right for one like Lizzie Hexam

indicators.note: letters that are not right are disordered, so they are rearranged here

explanation.surface: A pale room that isn't quite right for a Dickens heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Lizzie Hexam in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend rows her father's boat on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Lizzie Hexam rows the boat on the river, making her a female rower.

clue.text: Chap who wrote adventures is wasted on knight?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: a knight is a mounted horseman, a rider
wasted means gaunt and drawn, haggard

explanation.surface: A man who writes adventure stories goes to waste on a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines and She.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard was the author of adventure novels such as King Solomon's Mines.

clue.text: Revenge novel written about posh island queen

indicators.note: written about means the rearranged letters are set around the other pieces
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: U is upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A novel of revenge is penned about a classy island monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges REVENGE as GNEVERE, which goes around UI.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinevere is King Arthur's queen in the Arthurian legends.

clue.text: One supporting Dedalus works by a small hotel

parts.note: works means a factory, a plant

explanation.surface: Factories next to a little hotel support Joyce's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Dedalus carries an ashplant, a walking stick, in Joyce's Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a walking stick, which supports the walker; Stephen Dedalus carries one.

clue.text: Ambitious, like short chap like Hook Pan ultimately cuts

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the shortened word, going inside it
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Captain Hook is a pirate

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ambition is like a little fellow such as Hook, cut by Peter Pan in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Short PIRATE is PIRAT; the last letter of Pan goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is one who aspires, ambitious for a goal; here used adjectivally.

clue.text: Somehow resist racier woman chasing happiness

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A woman seeking joy fights off a racier rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Sister Carrie is Theodore Dreiser's novel of a country girl pursuing happiness in Chicago and New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreiser's heroine Carrie Meeber leaves home in search of a better, happier life.

clue.text: Men love to arrest wrong duke enamoured of page boy

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so the pieces hold the wrong inside them

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
love is zero in tennis, O
a wrong is a sin

explanation.surface: Soldiers and their sweethearts detain a misguided duke infatuated with a pageboy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night, Duke Orsino falls for Cesario, actually Viola disguised as a page.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Duke Orsino loves Cesario, the page who is really Viola.

clue.text: Not entirely kind and honourable serpentine beast

indicators.note: not entirely means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a kind is a type

explanation.surface: A creature is not wholly kind or noble.
explanation.walkthrough: Typhon is the monstrous serpent-headed giant of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhon in Greek myth is a giant with a hundred snake heads.

clue.text: Top-of-the-line American jeans shortened for writer

parts.note: primo is slang for first-rate, the very best

indicators.note: shortened means the brand name loses its final letter

parts.note: Levi's are American denim jeans

explanation.surface: Premium US denim cut down for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Primo Levi was the Italian chemist and author of If This Is a Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi was an Italian author famous for his Holocaust memoirs.

clue.text: Monster with yen to eat unknown noble writer

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the letters swallow the unknown

parts.note: an orc is a monster
Y is the abbreviation for the yen currency
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A monster with an appetite devours an unknown aristocrat author.
explanation.walkthrough: Baroness Orczy wrote The Scarlet Pimpernel.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroness Emma Orczy, a titled aristocrat, wrote The Scarlet Pimpernel.

clue.text: Ancient annual needing no introduction

indicators.note: an introduction is a beginning, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: annual means once a year, yearly

explanation.surface: A famous old yearbook that needs no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Early can mean belonging to a remote time, as in early man.

clue.text: Ace woman who loved Sikes is fabulous creature

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
in Oliver Twist, Nancy loves the brutal Bill Sikes

explanation.surface: A star lady devoted to a villain proves a legendary being.
explanation.walkthrough: Anancy is the spider trickster of West African and Caribbean folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anancy is the spider trickster of folk tales, and fables are such tales.

clue.text: A pound and Euro given to wealthy little king

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
E stands for European or Euro
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: Money in sterling and euros goes to a rich young ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Alberich is the dwarf king of the Nibelungs in Wagner's Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberich is the dwarf ruler of the Nibelungs, a small monarch.

clue.text: Quartet hysterically kidnapping Greek goddess

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer inside them, as a kidnapper holds a captive

explanation.surface: Four people wildly abduct a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethys is a Titaness of Greek myth, a sea deity.

clue.text: "That even in death his — breast / In such a dungeon could not rest" (Byron)

definitions.text: "That even in death his — breast / In such a dungeon could not rest" (Byron)

parts.words: "That even in death his — breast / In such a dungeon could not rest" (Byron)
parts.note: the missing adjective from The Prisoner of Chillon, describing a breast born to liberty

explanation.definitionFit: Byron's line describes a heart born to liberty, which a prison could not hold.
